assignments.title: Primary Source Report: Equiano and the Code Noir
assignments.html:
PRIMARY SOURCE REPORT
Equiano and the Code Noir
Sugar, Slaves, and the Atlantic World
16 points · text entry
≈ ≈ ≈
Before you start

Finish both lessons and read both sources first. Your notes from each page are kept in My Notebook, the button inside the page, so open it before you write. Then write your answers and submit them in this assignment.

QUESTIONS
1. Olaudah Equiano published his life story in 1789. The French crown issued the Code Noir in 1685. For each document, say who is speaking, who the audience is, and what the speaker wanted to achieve. How might these differences change what each document can teach us?
2. Choose one passage from Equiano's account of the voyage. Quote it in a few words, then explain in your own words what it shows about conditions aboard the ship and how he felt about them.
3. The Code Noir orders that enslaved people be baptized and limits some punishments, yet it also treats them as property that can be bought, sold, and inherited. Using evidence from both documents, explain how Equiano's account answers the idea that a person can be property.
4. A historian wants to learn how the slave system worked from day to day. Which of the two documents would you trust more for that purpose, and why? Name one thing the historian should check before relying on it.
GRADING RUBRIC (16 pts)
Criteria Excellent (4) Proficient (3) Developing (2) Beginning (1)
Understanding of the material
4 pts		 Reads both sources accurately and draws on specific details from each, along with what the week's lessons taught. Reads both sources accurately but uses few specific details, or leans on only one. Shows partial understanding of one or both sources, with some errors or vague claims. Misreads the sources or does not refer to them.
Quality of reasoning
4 pts		 Connects each claim to evidence and compares the sources with care. Explains why a speaker's purpose and position matter. Supports most claims with evidence. The comparison is sound but not fully developed. States conclusions with little support, or describes the sources without comparing them. Offers opinions without evidence from the sources.
Clarity and precision of expression
4 pts		 Writes in clear, well-organized sentences. Quotations are short, accurate, and introduced. Writing is clear with minor lapses in organization or precision. Writing is often unclear or disorganized, and quotations are unclear or misplaced. Writing is too unclear to follow.
Intellectual honesty
4 pts		 Names the limits of what each source can show and says what remains uncertain without overclaiming. Acknowledges at least one limit of the evidence. Mentions limits only in passing, or claims more than the sources allow. Treats each source as complete and beyond question.
Total:
16 pts total
SUBMISSION

Answer all four questions in complete sentences. Submit your answers in the text box on the Canvas assignment page. Aim for one solid paragraph for each question. You do not need an outside source. Your teacher will read your work and return a rubric score with a short comment.

quizzes.description:
MODULE INTRO
Sugar, Slaves, and the Atlantic World
2 questions · survey · one attempt
≈ ≈ ≈
Essential question for this week
How did sugar and the demand for labor bind Europe, Africa, and the Americas into one Atlantic world?
Instructions

Welcome to Sugar, Slaves, and the Atlantic World. This short check-in is not graded. Your answers help your teacher see where each student is starting, so answer honestly.

What you will be able to do

The Columbian Exchange and the Sugar Colonies

  • Describe what crossed the Atlantic in the Columbian Exchange and how it changed both sides.
  • Explain why sugar required the plantation system.
  • Trace the spread of sugar from the Mediterranean to Brazil and the Caribbean.

The Triangle Trade and the Middle Passage

  • Explain how the Atlantic slave trade worked and what role African states and European merchants played in it.
  • Describe the Middle Passage and the conditions enslaved people faced.
  • Trace the movement that ended the slave trade in the British Empire.

discussions.title: Discussion: Sugar and Slavery: Who Profited?
discussions.html:
DISCUSSION
Sugar and Slavery: Who Profited?
Sugar, Slaves, and the Atlantic World
10 points · threaded discussion
≈ ≈ ≈
Before you start

Finish both lessons first. Your notes from each lesson are kept in My Notebook, the button inside the lesson, so open it before you post. Then post your answer here and reply to one classmate.

DISCUSSION PROMPT

The sugar trade made fortunes, and it rested on the forced labor of millions of people. Many different groups took part in it, and the lessons show that they did not all have the same choices.

Choose one group that gained from the sugar and slave trades, such as planters, merchants and shipowners, governments, African rulers who sold captives, or buyers of sugar in Europe. Explain how that group gained and who bore the cost. Use at least two specific details from the lessons. Then say whether the people in your group could have understood what their gain cost others, and what that suggests about their responsibility.

Aim for about 150 to 200 words. Write about the people of the past with care and accuracy.

RESPOND TO A CLASSMATE

Reply to one classmate who chose a different group from yours. Do you agree with their reasoning? If so, strengthen it with a detail from the lessons that they did not use. If not, explain respectfully where it falls short, and point to a detail from the lessons that supports your view.

GRADING RUBRIC (10 pts)
Criteria Substantive (full credit) Thin (partial credit) Missing (no credit)
Claim and evidence
5 pts		 Names a group, explains how it gained and who paid, uses at least two specific details from the lessons, and gives a reasoned view of the group's responsibility. Names a group but gives only one detail, or stays general, or does not address responsibility. No post, or no group named.
Response to a classmate
5 pts		 Answers a specific point in a classmate's post and either strengthens it with a new detail or explains politely where it falls short. Replies in general terms, such as agreeing or disagreeing without a detail from the lessons. No reply.
10 pts total
